records.title: React DOM renderer requires a compatible React peer
records.summary: A React DOM 18.3.1 renderer paired with React 18.2.0 fails a strict npm peer-resolution check. In the pinned fixture, upgrading both React and React DOM to 18.3.1 passes the same installation check. This is evidence for the tested pair, not a universal version guarantee.
conditions: The project declares react-dom and react versions whose peer requirements must be reconciled.
The authorized scope permits checking or aligning the React renderer and the React package together.
actions: Read the actual react-dom target peerDependencies from the approved registry before changing declarations.
If the current React provider violates that peer range, propose an in-scope compatible React version; never silently change held declarations.
Run the receiving project's frozen install, renderer tests, and runtime acceptance on its final tree.
verification: Run a strict npm peer-resolution check against the exact approved versions.
Inspect the effective installed react/react-dom pair using npm ls.
Run the recipient project's React renderer and server-rendering tests.

actions: For the tested pair, set esbuild.jsx to transform while preserving the existing factory and fragment. Vite 8 deprecates this compatibility option.
Use explicit Oxc classic JSX settings only after the supported host range permits them. Verify peer ranges and receiving project behavior.
conditions: The Vite config sets esbuild.jsxFactory and jsxFragment to the non-React Html factory and Fragment without selecting a JSX runtime.
The receiving project uses classic JSX and verifies the exact transition from Vite 7.3.6 to 8.1.5.
records.summary: The classic Html factory and fragment settings in Fastify HTMX 0.4.1 work with Vite 7.3.6. With Vite 8.1.5, the original settings select a React JSX runtime. Explicitly selecting the classic transform restores the expected HTML on both tested versions.
records.title: Preserve classic JSX for Fastify HTMX on Vite 8.1.5
verification: Use a frozen install and build a representative JSX entry. Assert the emitted code renders the expected HTML.
Run the same control on every supported host Vite line before changing a reusable plugin.

records.title: Check generated Prisma enum values when moving to 7.0.0
records.summary: The pinned fixture emits mapped database values for UserPermissionRole on Prisma 7.0.0. Prisma 6.19.0 and 7.3.0 emit the schema member names. This finding applies to the tested generator versions.
conditions: The evaluated transition is @prisma/client 6.19.0 to 7.0.0 with the Prisma CLI at the same exact version.
The PostgreSQL schema has @map on enum members and application code observes or serializes the generated enum values.
actions: Check the exact CLI and client pins, then regenerate Prisma Client on a frozen lockfile.
Compare emitted values with application comparisons, fixtures, API responses and persisted database values before changing callers.
Test the actual selected Prisma patch. The 7.3.0 control restored the same generated values as 6.19.0.
verification: Check generated values using the recipient schema and exact CLI/client versions.
Test database round trips and the external representation of enum values in the receiving application when it exposes them.

actions: Keep the React runtime and renderer pair aligned. Reproduce the immediate read on the selected pair before changing the benchmark.
If the selected legacy fixture returns null before commit, wait for a bounded initial commit signal before starting benchmark timing. Fail when the expected static tree never commits.
conditions: The benchmark consumes toJSON() immediately after create() for a static host tree using the deprecated React Test Renderer.
The verified transition pairs React and react-test-renderer at 18.3.1 before the change and 19.3.0 after it. Reproduce the timing independently on any other pair.
Check that the benchmark measures serialization and permits waiting for fixture setup before timing starts.
records.summary: For the static legacy host-tree benchmark pattern, immediate toJSON() on the matched React and renderer 19.3.0 pair returned null in development and production. A bounded initial commit signal preserved the expected static JSON in both modes. The 18.3.1 pair returned that tree synchronously.
records.title: Read React Test Renderer JSON after the initial commit
verification: Freeze dependencies and verify the installed React and renderer versions.
Compare the exact static host tree with the React 18.3.1 synchronous control in development and production. Check that the benchmark still serializes the same fixture outside setup timing.
Run the receiving benchmark and compatibility tests.

actions: Run the Tailwind v4 CLI with --optimize when generating the CSS consumed by next build.
Regenerate the stylesheet in the build lifecycle when it is a precompiled app import.
conditions: Next.js is exactly 13.4.6 and its production CssMinimizerPlugin processes generated CSS.
The npm migration is Tailwind 3.3.2 to 4.0.0 with CLI, node and oxide all 4.0.0.
The generated stylesheet contains nested responsive rules such as lg:flex and lg:hidden. The evidence is scoped to their CSS behavior.
records.summary: Next 13.4.6 can merge nested responsive selectors that share a media query and lose distinct display declarations. On the checked npm transition, Tailwind 4.0.0 CLI --optimize flattens the selectors before Next minifies the CSS and restores desktop menu visibility.
records.title: Flatten Tailwind 4 responsive CSS before Next 13.4.6 production minification
verification: Inspect the real production CSS, then verify mobile hidden, desktop visible, and desktop hidden controls.
Retain the caller’s browser and runtime gates. A successful build alone does not detect this issue.

actions: Install the matching @tailwindcss/postcss adapter and use the Tailwind CSS import. Explicitly load any retained JS configuration.
Where the original default small shadow must remain, use shadow-xs and compare actual rendered shadow geometry. Verify custom radius independently.
Use outline-hidden where retaining the v3 forced-colors outline is required. Verify keyboard focus in the receiving application.
conditions: The npm project moves from Tailwind 3.4.4 to 4.3.3 and directly uses Tailwind as a PostCSS plugin.
Default utility names are present in rendered controls. Compare custom theme values before applying any codemod.
The checked compiler uses @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.3 and PostCSS 8.5.33; the v3 control uses PostCSS 8.4.38.
records.summary: Tailwind 4.3.3 rejects the v3 direct PostCSS plugin. After changing adapter and CSS entry, held shadow-sm compiles with different geometry. Select shadow-xs for the verified default shadow. For a custom rounded-sm, preserve the configured radius and verify its emitted value.
records.title: Check emitted styles after switching Tailwind to its v4 PostCSS adapter
verification: Use frozen installs and verify the compiler versions and applicable browser targets.
Inspect built CSS for shadow geometry, the configured radius and the forced-colors selector. Compare the receiving application in relevant browsers and themes.

actions: Check the declaration worker and its effective compiler options in addition to the top-level tsc version.

conditions: The source specifically upgrades TypeScript 5.9.2 to 6.0.3 with tsup 8.5.0 held and declarations enabled under pnpm.
The leaf emits through a bundler, legacy aliases are absent, and the actual tsup DTS worker uses TypeScript 6.0.3.
records.summary: tsup 8.5.0 inserts baseUrl into its declaration compiler options. On TypeScript 6.0.3 this can cause TS5101 even after a leaf tsconfig removes baseUrl and changes module resolution to bundler.
records.title: Check tsup’s implicit baseUrl when TypeScript 6 declaration builds fail
verification: Frozen install the exact graph. Run tsup through declaration emission; a JavaScript-only success or passing Vitest run leaves DTS unverified.
Exercise ESM and CJS entry points and declaration consumers with the receiving project’s export map, recording baseline failures.
Compare generated JavaScript and declarations against a clean baseline and verify downstream typecheck.

actions: Set build.lib.cssFileName to the basename used by the existing public stylesheet contract.

verification: Use a frozen dependency installation with compatible Vite plugin and Vue versions.
Run typecheck and production build. Inspect module membership and chunk import links in the emitted output.

actions: Read the chosen Vitest version peerDependencies and match the exact Vite version before updating declarations.

conditions: The current graph contains Vitest 2.1.2 with Vite 5.4.8 and the selected Vitest target is 5.0.0.

verification: Use strict npm peer resolution and compare installed Vite and Vitest versions with the intended pair.

verification: Install both graphs from frozen npm lockfiles.

records.title: Map values between same-named enums
records.summary: TypeScript 5.4 rejects assigning same-named enums when known member values differ.
conditions: Two distinct enum declarations have the same name and member names with different numeric values.
actions: Translate values explicitly at the boundary and handle every externally supplied value.
verification: Rerun the owning typecheck and test the mapping for each stable enum value.

records.title: Preserve intended writes to a filtered array
records.summary: TypeScript 5.5 narrows filter results for inferred type predicates. A later push of undefined can report TS2345.
conditions: An array filtered for defined values intentionally accepts undefined in later writes.
actions: Declare the result as the intended wider mutable array. If undefined is unintended, remove the write instead.
verification: Rerun typecheck and test the code that consumes the mutated result.

records.title: Check iterator completion before using value
records.summary: TypeScript 5.6 with strict mode types a built-in iterator's completion value as undefined.
conditions: The owning project enables strictBuiltinIteratorReturn and uses a built-in iterator's next().value without checking done.
actions: Branch on done and handle an exhausted iterator explicitly before reading value.
verification: Run typecheck and test both nonempty and exhausted iterators.

records.title: Initialize values read by nested functions
records.summary: TypeScript 5.7 diagnoses variables read by a nested function if they are never initialized.
conditions: A nested callback or function reads a strictly typed variable that was declared without an initializer and never assigned.
actions: Set a valid initial value or move the read after initialization.
verification: Run the owning typecheck and exercise the callback at its earliest invocation.

records.title: Use import attributes for NodeNext JSON imports
records.summary: TypeScript 5.8 reports TS2880 for a static JSON import with an import assertion under NodeNext.
conditions: An ESM file in a NodeNext project uses import ... assert { type: 'json' }.
actions: Replace assert with with and verify the runtime accepts import attributes.
verification: Run the owning typecheck and load the emitted module using the target Node version.

records.title: Use ArrayBuffer-backed bytes for Blob parts
records.summary: TypeScript 5.9 rejects a Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> in a BlobPart position.
conditions: The project types input as Uint8Array and passes it to a DOM API requiring ArrayBuffer-backed bytes.
actions: Keep the narrower buffer type if guaranteed, or copy the view with new Uint8Array(bytes) before creating the Blob.
verification: Rerun typecheck and verify that the Blob preserves the incoming byte range.

records.title: Replace baseUrl with explicit paths mappings
records.summary: TypeScript 7 rejects baseUrl, and a relative paths mapping resolves the same source module in the fixture.
conditions: An effective tsconfig uses baseUrl for nonrelative imports from the source tree.
actions: Remove baseUrl and its obsolete ignoreDeprecations override. Add explicit paths prefixes anchored at the owning tsconfig.
verification: Run typecheck and confirm the bundler or runtime resolves the same aliases.

records.title: Replace legacy route glob metacharacters
records.summary: Playwright 1.52 no longer treats ? and bracket classes as wildcards in route URL globs.
conditions: The suite relies on ? or a bracket class as a wildcard in page.route or browserContext.route.
actions: Replace the affected glob with a scoped RegExp and keep exact host and path constraints.
verification: Run the route test against a matching URL and a nearby URL that should not be intercepted.

records.title: Replace legacy route glob metacharacters in React CT
records.summary: Playwright React 17 component testing resolves the same 1.52 route matcher, which stops treating ? and [] as wildcards.
conditions: A React 17 component test uses page.route or browserContext.route with these glob metacharacters.
actions: Replace affected globs with scoped regular expressions.
verification: Run the component route test with matching and excluded URLs.

records.title: Replace removed Page accessibility snapshots
records.summary: Playwright 1.57 removes page.accessibility. Locator.ariaSnapshot sends a scoped selector and returns a YAML snapshot.
conditions: The suite calls page.accessibility.snapshot and uses its result to assert the roles and accessible names within a known region.
actions: Use Locator.ariaSnapshot for the same region and review the new snapshot expectations. Use a rule-based accessibility test for audit intent.
verification: Rebaseline the owning Playwright snapshot and verify its region, roles, and accessible names in the browser.

records.title: Import the public semver entrypoint
records.summary: The old semver/semver file resolves on the source and is absent on the target. The root entry still validates the same sample.
conditions: Code imports semver/semver directly.
actions: Import semver from the package root and use the public methods.
verification: Run the existing range and version tests against the replacement import.

records.title: Use the named LRUCache constructor
records.summary: Constructing the root CommonJS export fails on the target. The named LRUCache constructor stores and reads the fixture value.
conditions: Code constructs the value returned by require('lru-cache').
actions: Use the LRUCache named export and retain explicit cache bounds.
verification: Verify admission, eviction and TTL behavior used by the caller.

records.title: Read positional values from Commander args
records.summary: The old subcommand leaves a Command object in program.args. The target omits that object.
conditions: Handler code indexes program.args for the Command object after parsing a subcommand.
actions: Keep an explicit reference to the configured Command. Read the parsed positional inputs without relying on an embedded Command object.
verification: Test subcommand arguments and command-specific options through the CLI.

records.title: Register the formats referenced by Ajv schemas
records.summary: The old Ajv validates a sample with format: email. The target rejects compiling it until a format is registered.
conditions: Schemas use built-in v6 formats such as email and the upgraded validator uses strict defaults.
actions: Install a compatible ajv-formats release for standard formats or explicitly register project-owned formats with addFormat.
verification: Compile the receiving schemas and test valid and invalid boundary inputs for each format.

records.title: Replace safeLoad with load
records.summary: safeLoad parses the fixture on the source. The compatibility placeholder throws on v4 and load returns the expected mapping.
conditions: Code calls js-yaml safeLoad.
actions: Use load and retain explicit schemas if the application needs a non-default schema.
verification: Parse representative configuration, including custom tags and invalid YAML when present.

records.title: Use named ESM exports from js-yaml
records.summary: The ESM default object loads on the source. That import shape is absent on the target, where the named load function parses the sample.
conditions: ESM code accesses load through a default js-yaml import.
actions: Use import { load, dump } from 'js-yaml'. Review schema and custom tag migrations separately when used.
verification: Typecheck the changed imports and parse the YAML forms the project accepts.

records.title: Use the named v4 generator
records.summary: Calling the CommonJS package root generates a v4 UUID on the source. The root is no longer callable on the target. Its v4 export passes the same shape check.
conditions: The application calls the value returned by require('uuid') as a function.
actions: Import or destructure v4 from uuid and call it directly.
verification: Verify the version nibble, format and any fixed options used by tests.

records.title: Replace the removed uuid UMD asset
records.summary: The minified UMD artifact is shipped on the source and absent from the target. The target still exposes the v4 generator through the package entry.
conditions: HTML or an asset copy task references uuid/dist/umd/uuid.min.js.
actions: Bundle the v4 named export with the application's module toolchain, or build an explicit browser asset.
verification: Build the browser bundle and exercise the call site that used the UMD global.

records.title: Use the signal-exit onExit export
records.summary: The old CommonJS root is callable. The target root throws if called and exposes the onExit registration function.
conditions: Code directly calls the result of require('signal-exit').
actions: Use the named onExit export and retain the function it returns when the caller unregisters.
verification: Test registration and unregistration in a disposable subprocess.

records.title: Read Zod validation failures from issues
records.summary: The old implementation exposes errors on a failing safeParse. The target omits the alias and keeps the same field path in issues.
conditions: Code consumes ZodError.errors in response mapping or tests.
actions: Use error.issues and review any changes to issue codes and custom messages.
verification: Assert invalid-input paths and the emitted application error shape.

records.title: Replace mime.lookup with getType
records.summary: The old lookup method returns image/png for a file name. The target omits lookup and getType returns the same MIME type.
conditions: Code calls mime.lookup to infer a MIME type from a path or extension.
actions: Use mime.getType and handle null for unknown extensions according to the receiving contract.
verification: Test known and unknown extensions and the fallback Content-Type handling.

records.title: Select explicit body-parser middleware
records.summary: The combined bodyParser() entry creates middleware on the source and throws on the target. The target still constructs JSON-specific middleware.
conditions: Server setup calls bodyParser() without selecting a content-type parser.
actions: Configure bodyParser.json() and add urlencoded middleware only where needed. Audit parser limits and route order.
verification: Send representative JSON and form requests to covered routes, including malformed bodies.

records.title: Keep compressed data as bytes in pako
records.summary: A deflate request for a binary string returns a string on v1 and Uint8Array on v2. Passing the bytes to inflate round-trips the sample.
conditions: Code requests deflate output with to: 'string' and handles it as a binary string.
actions: Preserve Uint8Array through the compression pipeline. Encode bytes explicitly only at string-only boundaries.
verification: Round-trip representative binary and non-ASCII input through the consumer.

records.title: Register queue drain with a callback method
records.summary: The old queue fires an assigned drain callback. The target rejects assigning drain and fires the callback registered with drain(handler).
conditions: Code sets async.queue(...).drain to a function.
actions: Register the callback with queue.drain(handler). Retain any task-completion or error handlers.
verification: Enqueue a representative task and assert result and drain callback behavior.

records.title: Use Unicode calendar date tokens
records.summary: The old YYYY-MM-DD format emits a sample calendar date. V2 rejects the guarded tokens and yyyy-MM-dd produces the intended date.
conditions: Code passes YYYY or DD to date-fns format for calendar years or day of the month.
actions: Use yyyy for the calendar year and dd for the day of the month. Review week-year and day-of-year cases separately.
verification: Check calendar dates near year boundaries and formats that intentionally use week-numbering.

records.title: Use named date-fns addDays export
records.summary: The v2 addDays subpath loads as a callable function. V3 exposes the function as a named export, and the fixed import advances the sample day.
conditions: CommonJS directly calls the default value loaded from date-fns/addDays.
actions: Destructure addDays from the supported subpath or use the root named export.
verification: Test the migrated date calculation, especially time zone and daylight saving boundaries if relevant.

records.title: Create an XMLParser instance
records.summary: The source parses with the top-level parse function. The target omits it and an XMLParser instance reproduces the sample mapping.
conditions: Code calls fast-xml-parser.parse directly.
actions: Instantiate XMLParser with the required options and call parser.parse(xml).
verification: Compare parsed results for attributes, repeated elements, numbers and malformed documents.

records.title: Move pbjs scripts to the separate CLI package
records.summary: The source publishes a pbjs executable. The target no longer declares that command and retains the library entry.
conditions: A package or CI script gets pbjs from the protobufjs install.
actions: Install a compatible protobufjs-cli release explicitly and regenerate representative outputs.
verification: Compare generated messages and type declarations, and run a compile and encode-decode test.

records.title: Await the Terser minify result
records.summary: The source returns a result object synchronously. The old access on the target returns no code. Awaiting the result produces the sample output.
conditions: Build code reads terser.minify(...).code synchronously.
actions: Await minify and handle rejection. Update owning build hooks to return or await the promise.
verification: Run the release build and verify generated code, source maps and error propagation.

records.title: Use a supported jest-dom setup import
records.summary: The extend-expect subpath resolves on the source and fails on the target. The package root and matchers entry resolve on v6.
conditions: The test setup imports @testing-library/jest-dom/extend-expect.
actions: Import @testing-library/jest-dom in the Jest setup. For Jest globals disabled or Vitest, choose the matching documented setup subpath.
verification: Run a representative DOM matcher in the configured runner and check any TypeScript setup inclusion.

records.title: Import produce by name
records.summary: The CommonJS default produce function works on v9. Calling the target default throws, while the named produce updates the draft.
conditions: The caller imports Immer produce as a default export.
actions: Use the produce named export and retain existing draft update logic.
verification: Check the changed draft state and preservation of the input state.

records.title: Specify Reselect memoization when single-entry behavior matters
records.summary: With alternating parameters, v4 recomputes the first result and v5 default reuses it. Explicit lruMemoize reproduces the tested v4 behavior.
conditions: Selector logic or tests rely on a single cached parameter combination.
actions: Only where the previous contract matters, configure lruMemoize for memoize and argsMemoize.
verification: Check representative parameter sequences, recomputations and result reference identity.

records.title: Use string Redux action types
records.summary: The old store accepts a Symbol action type. The target rejects it, and a string action type reaches the same reducer logic.
conditions: Dispatched action.type values are Symbols or other non-string values.
actions: Replace non-string types with stable strings and update reducers, matchers and tests.
verification: Dispatch a representative migrated action and verify middleware and reducer behavior.

records.title: Replace getLCP with onLCP
records.summary: The old web-vitals root provides getLCP. The target no longer exports it and exposes onLCP.
conditions: The instrumentation imports getLCP from web-vitals.
actions: Register the reporting callback with onLCP and review the target metric payload shape.
verification: Verify one LCP report arrives with the expected shape in a receiving browser.

records.title: Replace FID collection with INP where intended
records.summary: The onFID subpath imports on v4 and is absent on v5. The target provides onINP.
conditions: Telemetry imports web-vitals/onFID.js and intends to report responsiveness.
actions: Use onINP for interaction responsiveness and update the dashboard to track INP as a different metric.
verification: Verify the replacement event in a browser and keep FID and INP series distinct.

records.title: Preserve Vite client defaults beside custom resolve conditions
records.summary: Vite 6 stops appending some client conditions internally when a custom list is set. The fixture checks that the explicit configuration restores browser while retaining the custom condition.
conditions: The Vite configuration overrides resolve.conditions for client dependency resolution.
actions: Merge defaultClientConditions from vite into the custom list. Evaluate SSR separately with defaultServerConditions when the project customizes SSR conditions.
verification: Build the client with a dependency that uses browser and custom conditional exports and inspect the entry selected.

records.title: Use parameter defaults in React function components
records.summary: With the JSX runtime, the old function defaultProps supplies a button label on the source and is ignored on the target. A parameter default restores it.
conditions: A function component rendered through the modern JSX runtime relies on defaultProps for an omitted prop.
actions: Move the fallback into a destructured parameter default. Keep intentional caller overrides.
verification: Render the component both without the prop and with an explicit prop value.

records.title: Switch Tailwind to its v4 PostCSS adapter

actions: Use @tailwindcss/postcss@4.0.0 for the tested version and replace the legacy entry with @import 'tailwindcss'. The official upgrade tool is optional after reviewing its supported inputs.
verification: Build CSS and compare emitted utilities and browser behavior. Review any upgrade-tool diff before applying it.

records.title: Pass an explicit initial value to useRef

actions: Pass undefined to preserve an undefined initial ref. For matching calls, review the optional types-react-codemod@3.5.0 useRef-required-initial transform in dry-run mode before applying it.
verification: Review the codemod source and diff for aliases or shadowing. Typecheck the changed project. The fixture checks the manual equivalent.

records.title: Update headers through AxiosHeaders on Axios 1
records.summary: The Axios 1 request interceptor rejects a plain headers object at typecheck. AxiosHeaders.set preserves caller headers at the adapter boundary.
conditions: The owning request interceptor assigns a new object to config.headers.
actions: Use config.headers.set for the affected headers, keeping unrelated values and existing conditions.
Review whether intentionally removed headers need an explicit deletion.
verification: Run the typecheck and inspect the adapter input for the updated and unrelated caller headers.

records.title: Use object signatures in TanStack Query v5
records.summary: TanStack Query 5.75.5 rejects the old positional hook and client fetch. Passing queryKey and queryFn together preserves the rendered result and cache key.
conditions: A React Query v4 hook or QueryClient method still relies on positional arguments.
actions: Convert the hook and any nested client fetch to object forms and preserve the existing key, fetcher and enabled options.
Check any dynamically constructed options for accidental query-key changes.
verification: Render a cached or disabled state and verify the resolved data under the intended key.

records.title: Preserve relative sibling links under React Router 7 splats
records.summary: React Router 7.18.4 includes the splat portion in relative resolution. Splitting the route and adjusting the link restores the intended sibling href.
conditions: A multi-segment splat such as dashboard/* contains relative links intended to target siblings.
actions: Separate the named parent and the splat child, then make the sibling link parent-relative.
Preserve absolute links and verify any index route separately.
verification: Render or follow a relative link from a populated splat and confirm the intended sibling URL.

records.title: Await route params and searchParams on Next.js 16
records.summary: Reading params synchronously on Next.js 16.4.2 makes a valid dynamic route return 404 in the fixture. Awaiting both inputs restores the route and query mode.
conditions: An App Router server page reads properties from params or searchParams synchronously.
actions: Make the page async and await params and searchParams before validating or using their fields.
Check metadata, layouts and route handlers for equivalent synchronous access.
verification: Request a valid deep link with and without a query parameter. Confirm that an invalid ID still produces 404.

records.title: Use mount and unmount at Svelte 5 client entry points
records.summary: A Svelte 5.0.0 component compiled with the default API rejects construction with new. Mounting through the runtime preserves the target, props and teardown.
conditions: A client entry manually constructs a Svelte component at an empty DOM target.
actions: Import mount and pass the existing target and props. Use unmount when the integration manages teardown.
Review existing SSR hydration separately before replacing its startup call.
verification: Check the component renders with a supplied prop and removes its DOM on teardown.

records.title: Use the Redux Toolkit builder for extraReducers
records.summary: The old object-valued extraReducers fails store initialization in Redux Toolkit 2 development mode. The builder callback preserves the three async thunk states.
conditions: A slice uses an extraReducers object keyed by computed async-thunk action types.
actions: Convert the object to a builder callback and register existing handlers with addCase and their matching action creators.
The builder works on both pinned versions, so the code change can ship before the version bump.
verification: Dispatch the success and rejection cases. Assert pending, fulfilled and rejected state and preserve unrelated state.

records.title: Preserve an Express 5 catch-all that includes the root
records.summary: The bare Express 4 wildcard fails to register on Express 5. The optional named wildcard preserves the root and nested fallback.
conditions: The application registers a bare '*' or '/*' catch-all and its fallback is expected to include the root.
actions: Use /{*splat} for a root-inclusive fallback and keep it after specific routes.
If handlers read wildcard captures, check the new capture key and array representation.
verification: Request the root, a nested miss and a known route. Compare the actual fallback response body as well as its status.

records.title: Remove the callback from Mongoose 9 pre-validate middleware
records.summary: Keeping a Mongoose 8 pre-validate callback makes valid input fail in Mongoose 9. A synchronous hook preserves the original validation rule.
conditions: A schema registers pre('validate') middleware that calls next.
actions: For synchronous logic, remove the next parameter and call, preserving the document context and validation rule.
Use a returned promise for async pre middleware and preserve errors. Confirm the Node.js version meets the target engine (at least 20.19.0 for 9.11.3).
verification: Await document.validate() for a normal input, an equality boundary and a rejected value. Check the field-specific error.

negativeControls.name: callback-fails-valid-input
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: await assert.rejects(valid.validate(), /next is not a function/)

records.title: Move Storybook play helpers to storybook/test
records.summary: The old @storybook/test import cannot resolve after that dependency is removed in the Storybook 9 upgrade. The storybook/test subpath preserves a play-style interaction.
conditions: The upgraded workspace removes its standalone @storybook/test dependency and still imports it from stories or helpers.
actions: Move imports of expect, fn, userEvent and within to storybook/test in the owning workspace.
Remove the old dependency once the workspace has no imports that still need it.
verification: Build the workspace Storybook and run a representative play test using an accessible query, click and handler assertion.

records.title: Preserve HTTP mock behavior when moving to MSW 2
records.summary: MSW 2 rejects the held rest.get handler. Using http.get and HttpResponse.json preserves the fixture's payload, status and response headers.
conditions: Tests register MSW 1 HTTP handlers through rest and return composed status, JSON and header transformers.
actions: Use http handlers and their params argument. Pass the original body, status and headers to HttpResponse.json.
Keep any project-specific setup, polyfills and worker checks in scope when verifying the receiving test suite.
verification: Run a representative mock request for both success and error. Assert JSON, status, headers and the unhandled route behavior.

records.title: Use an explicit Content Layer loader on Astro 6
records.summary: Astro 6 rejects the legacy src/content/config.ts in the fixture. An explicit loader and migrated entry consumers restore the rendered route.
conditions: The site has a legacy src/content/config.ts collection and reads its entries to build static pages.
actions: Move collection configuration to src/content.config.ts and add the appropriate loader.
Replace legacy slug and entry.render() reads as needed. Compare output paths for custom slugs and nested IDs.
verification: Build the site and verify the same entry URLs, rendered Markdown and an unrelated static page.

records.title: Use branch callbacks in Yup 1 conditional schemas
records.summary: Passing schemas directly to then or otherwise fails on Yup 1. Applying callbacks to the incoming schema preserves both conditional presence and the fixture's shared restriction.
conditions: A Yup when() call supplies schema objects directly as then or otherwise.
actions: Return the intended schema from a callback. Extend the incoming schema to retain its existing validators.
Preserve any intentionally separate branch constraints when moving them into callbacks.
verification: Validate both branches, a missing required value and an unsupported present value.

negativeControls.name: held-schema-branch-rejected
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.rejects(async () => held.validate(valid), /branch is not a function/)

records.title: Migrate named React Hook Form inputs with the v7 registration codemod
records.summary: A v6 ref registration call fails on the v7 runtime. The official named-field transform preserves validation and submitted data for the fixture.
conditions: A JSX input has a literal name attribute and a ref registration from a destructured React Hook Form useForm result.
actions: Apply the official v7/update-register transform from @hookform/codemod 1.0.0 on matching fields.
Inspect spread-only names, wrapper components and forwarded refs manually.
verification: Review the codemod source diff for retained names and options. Run required validation and submit a populated form.

records.title: Qualify shared Sass variables when replacing @import with @use
records.summary: Sass 1.80.0 warns on legacy @import and fails when the deprecation is fatal. A namespaced @use preserves the fixture CSS and passes strict compilation.
conditions: An SCSS entry imports shared Sass variables with @import and uses them without a module namespace.
actions: Load the module with @use and qualify the shared variables using its namespace.
Check module load order and repeat emissions if more than one module writes CSS.
verification: Compare generated CSS and run a focused build with the import deprecation treated as an error.

negativeControls.name: legacy-import-rejected-in-strict-mode
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.throws(() => compile(after, legacy, true), /Sass @import rules are deprecated/)

records.title: Use named imports when upgrading date-fns to v3
records.summary: With synthetic default imports disabled, date-fns 3.6.0 declarations reject held default subpath imports. The JavaScript fallback still runs. Root named imports pass the fixture type check and preserve its outputs across both versions.
conditions: An ES module imports date-fns function subpaths through default bindings and needs its declarations checked without synthetic default imports.
actions: Switch the affected default subpath imports to named imports from the date-fns root.
The same named imports pass on 2.30.0, so the code edit can be verified before the dependency update.
verification: Type-check and bundle the owning entry. Compare representative date and duration outputs.

records.title: Await user-event 14 typing and focus transitions
records.summary: An immediate read after an unawaited v14 action sees stale state. Awaited actions preserve the typed value and the final focus.
conditions: A test calls user-event type or tab and reads value or focus before the action completes.
actions: Await the affected interactions before asserting their effects. A setup session can share interaction state across calls.
Direct calls can also be awaited. Check fake timers independently if the test uses them.
verification: Check the entered value and tab order after awaiting the interaction.

records.title: Replace Pino's removed prettyPrint option with a transport
records.summary: The retained prettyPrint option prevents Pino 10.1.0 logger construction. A worker transport preserves readable output in the fixture.
conditions: A Pino logger passes prettyPrint to its constructor and the upgraded environment still needs readable output.
actions: Move the formatting options to a pino-pretty transport and preserve the desired destination.
Keep plain JSON sinks and check worker resolution and shutdown in the receiving deployment.
verification: Emit a sample event, wait for the worker to drain, and check severity, message and structured fields.

negativeControls.name: legacy-prettyprint-option-rejected
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.match(held.stderr, /prettyPrint option is no longer supported/i)

records.title: Move Apollo Client 4 React bindings out of the root import
records.summary: Root React imports fail to render on Apollo Client 4. The React entry point restores the fixture's cache-only markup.
conditions: A React component imports ApolloProvider or useQuery from the @apollo/client root.
actions: Move React imports to @apollo/client/react and keep ApolloClient, InMemoryCache and gql at the root.
Satisfy the target version's RxJS peer requirement and verify other changed entry points separately.
verification: Render a representative query and check data and loading behavior. Include a cache-only test for SSR where applicable.

records.title: Use Material UI 7 Grid and retain responsive sizes
records.summary: The v6 Grid2 entry point fails on v7. The new Grid with a responsive size object preserves the expected width rules.
conditions: A project imports the v6 Grid2 entry point or sends legacy item and breakpoint props to the v7 Grid.
actions: Import the v7 component from @mui/material/Grid. Keep an existing size object or convert legacy xs and sm props to it.
Check the owning layout's spacing and custom breakpoints.
verification: Check width at the base breakpoint and at sm, along with the rendered content.

records.title: Read parsed Commander options with opts()
records.summary: Commander 7's default storage no longer exposes parsed options as Command properties. opts() preserves explicit flags and defaults across this transition.
conditions: A CLI reads parsed flags directly on its Command instance and relies on default option storage.
actions: Use program.opts() at the readers of the parsed options.
The fixture verifies the edit on both pinned versions, so the code migration can be tested before the bump.
verification: Exercise explicit values, flags and default values with no arguments.

negativeControls.name: default-storage-omits-command-properties
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.deepEqual(parse(after, args, true), { format: undefined, verbose: false })

records.title: Register Sentry BrowserTracing with the v8 factory
records.summary: The legacy tracing entry point is missing when the old package is removed. The Sentry React factory registers BrowserTracing and preserves local event dispatch.
conditions: Sentry initialization imports BrowserTracing via @sentry/tracing and the v8 upgrade removes that dependency.
actions: Use browserTracingIntegration() from @sentry/react and review the integration options.
Check the React peer range before the upgrade and verify routing instrumentation and sampling separately.
verification: Confirm the integration registers and a test event reaches a local transport before using the real service.

records.title: Await the named glob export for workspace matching
records.summary: glob 10 uses a named Promise API. The old CommonJS module call fails, and passing a callback to the named export does not process the result. On Windows, the default result uses backslashes where v7 emitted slashes.
conditions: A CommonJS script calls require('glob') as a function and handles file matches in a callback.
actions: Destructure glob from require('glob'), await glob(pattern, options), and propagate matching errors to the existing handler.
Keep async error handling. If downstream consumers require slash-delimited paths, pass posix: true and check the returned spelling.
verification: Compare the selected workspace files including nested matches and excluded paths.

negativeControls.name: old-commonjs-call-fails-on-target
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.throws(() => target(pattern, { cwd }, () => {}), /target is not a function/)

records.title: Await Redis 4 connection before running commands
records.summary: The old client connects during creation. The v4 client rejects commands before connect(). Awaiting the connection restores the initial PING.
conditions: Server startup calls createClient() and relies on implicit connection before issuing Redis commands.
actions: Register connection error handling and await client.connect() before the application issues Promise-based commands.
Review client configuration and verify connection failure and shutdown with the actual Redis service.
verification: Start the affected code path and confirm Redis reaches readiness and PING returns PONG.

negativeControls.name: v4-rejects-command-before-connect
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: await assert.rejects(client.ping(), { name: 'Error', message: 'The client is closed' })

records.title: Keep NgModule declarations non-standalone in Angular 19
records.summary: Angular 19 treats components as standalone when the flag is omitted. Existing NgModule declarations then fail compilation. Explicit standalone: false preserves the Angular 18 setup.
conditions: An NgModule declares a component whose decorator omits standalone, and that component should remain module-declared.
actions: Set standalone: false on affected declarations that stay in an NgModule.
Upgrade the compiler packages with core and check the target compiler's TypeScript peer range.
verification: Compile the affected NgModules and check that they still accept their declarations.

records.title: Convert single-emission RxJS observables with firstValueFrom
records.summary: RxJS 7 adds undefined to the return type of toPromise(). firstValueFrom restores a strict Promise<T> for a single-emission source, but empty and multiple streams behave differently.
conditions: A call to toPromise() converts a source known to emit one value into a non-optional Promise result.
actions: Use firstValueFrom(source) when the first emission is the intended result.
Check empty behavior explicitly. Choose lastValueFrom for the last result when the source completes.
verification: Type-check the affected Promise return and test representative single, empty and multiple-emission paths.

records.title: Use an esbuild build context for watch mode
records.summary: At 0.17.0, esbuild removed the watch option from build(). context.watch() preserves edit-driven rebuilds, and context.dispose() stops the watcher.
conditions: The update crosses esbuild 0.17.0 from an earlier release and an affected JavaScript build() call passes watch.
actions: Use an awaited context.watch() in the watch branch and dispose the context on shutdown.
Keep one-shot build() calls without watch. If startup requires the first artifact, wait for completion explicitly.
verification: Check the initial output, edit an input, and confirm the watcher emits the updated bundle.

records.title: Register standard date formats on Ajv 8 before compiling
records.summary: Ajv 8 rejects the unregistered date format under strict defaults. ajv-formats restores validation and its full date check can reject dates the old default accepted.
conditions: Project schemas use format: date and rely on Ajv 6's built-in formats.
actions: Register a compatible ajv-formats plugin on the Ajv instance before compiling the schema.
Check persisted and user-entered dates that may have passed the old validator.
verification: Validate a real leap day, malformed input and a non-leap February 29.

records.title: Enable legacy Socket.IO handshakes during a v4 server rollout
records.summary: Socket.IO 4 rejects the tested v2 polling client by default. allowEIO3 restores its handshake and event acknowledgement while the tested v4 client keeps working.
conditions: Socket.IO server upgrades from v2 to v4 while deployed Socket.IO v2 clients still connect to it.
actions: Set allowEIO3: true on the upgraded Socket.IO server for the staged client rollout.
After the old clients have migrated, remove the compatibility setting and verify the deployed transports.
verification: Connect pinned old and new clients and round-trip an acknowledged event through the expected transport.

records.title: Use the GraphQL argument object for execution
records.summary: GraphQL 16 only accepts the graphql() argument object. Passing named fields preserves query execution on both pinned releases.
conditions: The project invokes graphql() with positional arguments instead of an execution options object.
actions: Move the schema, query source and any supplied root, context, variables and operation name into the argument object.
The tested object form works on the old and target versions, so the edit can land before the dependency bump.
verification: Run a request with variables, a selected operation and a context-dependent resolver and compare the response.

records.title: Move vitePreprocess to the Vite plugin in SvelteKit 2
records.summary: SvelteKit 2 no longer exports vitePreprocess from @sveltejs/kit/vite. The Vite plugin export restores preprocessing and component compilation.
conditions: The Svelte config imports vitePreprocess from @sveltejs/kit/vite.
actions: Import vitePreprocess from @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte and align the plugin with the target Svelte and Vite versions.
Keep the project's preprocessing options when switching import paths.
verification: Preprocess and compile a component that uses an affected language such as TypeScript.

negativeControls.name: kit-vite-v2-missing-vitepreprocess-export
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.match(held.stderr, /does not provide an export named 'vitePreprocess'/)

records.title: Restore Marked heading IDs with the GFM extension
records.summary: The Marked 17 renderer leaves intra-document links in place while dropping heading IDs. The GFM heading extension restores the tested anchor IDs, including repeated headings.
conditions: Links, bookmarks or a table of contents depend on heading IDs emitted by the old Marked renderer.
actions: Register a compatible marked-gfm-heading-id extension on the renderer.
Compare existing slug conventions and prefixes for representative documents.
verification: Render duplicate headings and confirm an intra-document link points to the matching ID.

records.title: Migrate Biome 2 import assist and file exclusions
records.summary: Biome 2 rejects legacy organizer and ignore keys. The pinned CLI migrates them and keeps import sorting and the tested file exclusion.
conditions: The Biome 1 configuration uses organizeImports and files.ignore to sort selected imports while omitting generated source files.
actions: Run the locally installed Biome 2.0.4 CLI as biome migrate --write from the affected config root.
Inspect the converted assist action and glob exclusions before applying other fixes.
verification: Run Biome on an included source and an excluded generated file. Confirm imports sort and the excluded file stays unchanged.

records.title: Create stopped node-cron 4 tasks with createTask()
records.summary: node-cron 4 schedule() ignores scheduled: false and executes on its schedule before an explicit start. createTask() restores the deferred startup contract.
conditions: A task uses schedule(..., { scheduled: false }) and must wait for an explicit application start.
actions: Use createTask() for the deferred task and retain the explicit start() call.
Keep automatically started jobs on schedule() and verify each job's runtime options.
verification: Observe a schedule tick before activation, then start the task and confirm its callback runs.

records.title: Use Faker number.int for bounded integer data
records.summary: Faker 9 removes datatype.number. number.int preserves the tested bounds and within-version seed repeatability. The seeded sequence changes across the pinned releases.
conditions: The project uses faker.datatype.number with explicit bounds to generate integer data.
actions: Use faker.number.int with the same integer bounds.
Review tests or snapshots that depend on exact seeded values across versions.
verification: Check bounds, integer output and repeatability after resetting the seed on the target version.

negativeControls.name: held-faker-datatype-number-is-removed
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.throws(() => legacyDraw(after), /datatype.number is not a function/)

records.title: Use toZonedTime for date-fns-tz 3 display conversion
records.summary: date-fns-tz 3 removes utcToZonedTime. toZonedTime preserves the tested local display values around daylight-saving boundaries.
conditions: The project uses utcToZonedTime to render UTC instants as local wall time.
actions: Rename the import and call to toZonedTime. If date-fns is still 2.x, include a compatible 3.x or 4.x peer in the upgrade.
Keep the original instant for ordering or identity when local times can repeat.
verification: Compare local display values around both daylight-saving transitions in the affected time zone.

records.title: Move the tRPC 11 transformer into the HTTP batch link
records.summary: tRPC 11 leaves the tested SuperJSON response serialized when the transformer stays at client root. The HTTP batch link transformer restores the Date.
conditions: The tRPC client supplies SuperJSON in its root options and makes requests through httpBatchLink.
actions: Move transformer: superjson into httpBatchLink options and keep the server transformer configured.
Keep the tRPC client and server versions compatible and review any other active transport links.
verification: Query a Date field and compare its runtime type and exact UTC timestamp.

records.title: Load Chalk 5 default export from CommonJS with dynamic import
records.summary: Chalk 5 is ESM. The retained require() either fails or returns a module namespace without direct color methods. Importing the default export preserves the tested output.
conditions: A CommonJS CLI reads color helpers directly from require('chalk') and needs to retain its CommonJS entry point.
actions: Load the default export with native dynamic import before invoking color helpers.
Inspect transpiled output so that the import stays dynamic on supported runtimes.
verification: Smoke-test both plain and ANSI-colored output on the actual CLI runtime.

records.title: Declare jest-environment-jsdom for Jest 28 DOM tests
records.summary: Jest 28 no longer brings the jsdom environment into the tested installation. The matching direct environment dependency restores test initialization.
conditions: The project uses testEnvironment: jsdom or a jsdom environment annotation.
actions: Add a compatible jest-environment-jsdom development dependency alongside the Jest update.
Keep the project environment selection and review test transformers separately.
verification: Run a representative DOM test and check that the jsdom environment initializes.

negativeControls.name: jest28-install-without-jsdom-fails-environment-selection
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.match(held.output, /Test environment jest-environment-jsdom cannot be found/)

records.title: Ember 7 removes legacy application test-helper injection
records.summary: The shipped test extension and its TestableApp types disappear by ember-source 7.2.0. A pinned consumer typecheck passed on 6.10.1, rejected the legacy setup with 7.2.0, and passed on both after switching to explicit helpers.
conditions: The test setup calls Application#injectTestHelpers() or imports TestableApp from ember-testing/lib/ext/application.
actions: Remove legacy global helper injection and import the helpers used by the tests from @ember/test-helpers.
Keep the modern setApplication(app) setup. If an intentional debug global is still needed, expose only that named helper explicitly.
verification: Run the project's typecheck against the actual target Ember and compatible @ember/test-helpers.
Run representative application tests and look for remaining uses of injected globals.

records.title: Chokidar 4 drops glob arguments to watch
records.summary: Chokidar 4.0.3 reported no initial add events for the suffix glob that Chokidar 3.6.0 handled. Watching the root directory with a file-only filter recovered the nested matching file and kept unrelated files out.
conditions: Project code passes a glob directly to chokidar.watch() rather than expanding it before the call.
actions: Watch explicit root directories. For a simple suffix glob, ignore files with other suffixes while keeping directories traversable.
For path-sensitive patterns or exclusions, preserve their meaning with a dedicated matcher or expansion and keep the original watch roots.
verification: Check initial discovery for a nested match, an excluded file and an out-of-root file.
Exercise live create, edit and removal events in the receiving environment when the application relies on them.

records.title: Preserve the lowercase hex color rule after the Stylelint 16 plugin migration
records.summary: Stylelint 16.2.0 treats color-hex-case and stylistic/color-hex-case as unknown with the replacement plugin. @stylistic/color-hex-case kept lowercase enforcement for the Wikimedia-backed test.
conditions: The project's style rules require lowercase hex, and its configuration uses color-hex-case or stylistic/color-hex-case.
actions: If the policy should remain, request scope for a compatible @stylistic/stylelint-plugin and configure @stylistic/color-hex-case with the lower option.
Replace the legacy namespace and check inherited config and plugin peers before removing the old plugin.
verification: Lint an uppercase value expecting a casing warning and a lowercase value expecting no warning.
Run the receiving repository's Stylelint task against its actual presets and file types.

records.title: Preserve middleware order when webpack-dev-server 5 removes the legacy hook
records.summary: Version 5.2.2 rejects onBeforeSetupMiddleware. In the pinned local HTTP fixture, returning the middleware array from setupMiddlewares retained both a custom response and a real Webpack bundle.
conditions: The project sets devServer.onBeforeSetupMiddleware and needs to preserve its hook behavior on the target version.
actions: Move the callback to setupMiddlewares and return the middleware array. Prepend custom middleware that must run before the built-in stack.
Preserve the original hook side effects and any separate startup requirements within the approved scope.
verification: Start the receiving dev server and verify the custom response, hook invocation count and compiled-bundle fallback.
Check any project-specific proxy, HTTPS and HMR behavior separately.

records.title: Keep the matching native package when upgrading to Rollup 4
records.summary: Rollup 4.0.0 could not load on the tested platforms when npm omitted optional packages. Including the platform package from the same locked installation restored the Rollup bundle.
conditions: The npm build runs Rollup 4 and its native artifact for the target OS, architecture and libc is missing after install.
The fixture covers Windows x64 and glibc Linux x64 with the matching package present in the target lock.
actions: If policy permits, include optional packages in the frozen npm install and keep the platform artifact selected by Rollup.
Inspect the target lock for the matching native package if including optional dependencies does not install it.
verification: Check that the expected native package is installed on the build platform.
Run the actual project build with the target Rollup version.

records.title: Keep legacy Fancybox galleries working during a jQuery 4 upgrade
records.summary: Fancybox 3.5.7 calls $.isArray when opening a gallery. The tested jQuery 4.0.0 transition throws until jquery-migrate 4.0.2 is loaded before Fancybox.
conditions: The application keeps @fancyapps/fancybox 3.5.7 and uses its jQuery-backed gallery while updating jQuery to 4.x.
Inspect both the entry point that supplies window.jQuery and the legacy plugin's actual loading order.
actions: If the project must retain Fancybox 3, load jquery-migrate@4.0.2 after the same jQuery 4 instance and before Fancybox. Keep the bridge scoped to entry points using the plugin.
Remove the compatibility dependency after upgrading or replacing the legacy plugin and verifying the gallery.
verification: Open a representative gallery, verify its configured content renders, and close it.
Run the production build and check the receiving browser for load order, keyboard focus and media behavior.

records.title: Preserve Markdown wrapper classes when updating to React Markdown 10
records.summary: React Markdown 10.0.0 renders the Markdown content without the wrapper created by the old className prop. An explicit wrapper restored the exact React server markup from 9.0.3.
conditions: A React Markdown 9 call sets className and depends on the generated element for styling or selectors.
actions: Move the class to the containing element, or add a wrapper at the same position when the old call supplied the wrapper.
Preserve the Markdown children, existing wrapper attributes and selectors tied to DOM structure.
verification: Compare the rendered Markdown contents and classed parent element before and after the change.
Run the receiving page test and check layout or CSS selectors that use the parent class.

records.title: Load the jest-dom 6 root entry in test setups with global expect
records.summary: With the same global expect setup, the 5.17.0 extend-expect import registers matchers, 6.1.5 rejects that subpath, and the 6.1.5 root import restores matcher registration.
conditions: The test setup imports @testing-library/jest-dom/extend-expect and its runner provides global expect.
actions: Replace the extend-expect import with @testing-library/jest-dom in the existing test setup.
When the runner does not provide global expect, use the runner-specific entry supported by the selected release.
verification: Run the project test setup and an existing DOM matcher assertion under the receiving runner.
Check runner globals and TypeScript setup if matcher types are missing.

records.title: Preserve the virtual console error policy when moving to jsdom 27
records.summary: jsdom 27.0.0 removes VirtualConsole.sendTo. Changing the method alone leaves omitJSDOMErrors ineffective. Using forwardTo with jsdomErrors set to none preserved page logs, the explicit jsdomError listener and the suppressed default forwarding in the pinned replay.
conditions: The project or an installed adapter calls sendTo on a jsdom VirtualConsole while upgrading to jsdom 27.
Map the suppression option only when the old code set omitJSDOMErrors to true, and keep any existing jsdomError listener.
actions: For application-owned code, use VirtualConsole.forwardTo. Replace omitJSDOMErrors: true with jsdomErrors: 'none' when preserving suppression.
If the call is inside an installed test adapter, verify the adapter release supports the target jsdom or retain the working jsdom version until it can be upgraded.
verification: Run the test setup through the actual runner and confirm a representative page message still reaches the configured sink.
Trigger a jsdom error and verify the explicit handler and default forwarding match the original policy.

negativeControls.name: legacy-method-rejected
negativeControls.fixtureAssertion: assert.throws(() => replay(after, legacy), /sendTo is not a function/);

records.title: Await Prettier 3 format results across npm, Yarn PnP and pnpm
records.summary: The retained direct consumer calls prettier.format with the built-in Babel parser and immediately trims the returned string. It works with Prettier 2.8.8 and throws TypeError with 3.0.0. Awaiting format before trimming preserves the exact formatted output under all three pinned package managers. Invalid JavaScript still rejects, and removing the async repair reproduces the failure.
conditions: The retained dependency graph changes Prettier 2.8.8 and Zod 3.25.76 together to Prettier 3.0.0 and Zod 4.6.7; the checks call each package's public API directly.
Replay uses Node 24.18.0 with npm 11.16.0 node_modules, Yarn 4.12.0 Plug'n'Play, or pnpm 10.29.3 with its isolated node_modules layout and each manager's retained frozen lockfile.
The Yarn execution uses its CommonJS and ESM PnP loaders with no arm node_modules; every package must resolve from the selected arm, even when matching-version packages exist in a parent directory.
The application uses the programmatic format API with parser: 'babel' and performs a string operation on its result; this case does not test third-party plugins, editor integrations or CLI behavior.
actions: Make the formatting consumer async and await prettier.format(source, options) before trimming, serializing or returning the resulting text.
Propagate the asynchronous boundary through the actual caller and preserve syntax-error rejection instead of replacing failures with successful output.
Install with the recipient's frozen lockfile and execute through its selected manager; use yarn node for the retained PnP case so both CommonJS and ESM resolution use the arm's loaders.
Treat this as advisory migration evidence. Verify the recipient's actual parser, options, plugins, entry points and supported platforms before accepting its final tree.
verification: Run both exact package graphs under each manager; assert the old sync consumer passes before the upgrade, fails afterward, and the awaited consumer yields 'const data = { key: 1 };'.
Check that malformed JavaScript such as 'const =' still rejects with the formatter's syntax diagnostic after the repair.
Confirm a restored synchronous consumer fails on the target and a missing arm or omitted PnP loader is rejected despite an accessible matching-version parent package.
Compare repaired target output to baseline output, retain unchanged manifests and frozen locks, then run the recipient's formatting and downstream caller tests.

records.title: Preserve Zod validation failures with issues across three package managers
records.summary: A direct safeParse consumer reads error.errors[0].message to form an invalid-email response. The pinned Zod 4.6.7 graph throws TypeError on that failure path while valid input still succeeds. Reading error.issues preserves the baseline invalid response, issue path and successful parsed data under npm, Yarn PnP and pnpm. The fixture calls a response-producing function; it does not run an HTTP server.
conditions: The retained dependency graph changes Prettier 2.8.8 and Zod 3.25.76 together to Prettier 3.0.0 and Zod 4.6.7; the checks call each package's public API directly.
Replay uses Node 24.18.0 with npm 11.16.0 node_modules, Yarn 4.12.0 Plug'n'Play, or pnpm 10.29.3 with its isolated node_modules layout and each manager's retained frozen lockfile.
The Yarn execution uses its CommonJS and ESM PnP loaders with no arm node_modules; every package must resolve from the selected arm, even when matching-version packages exist in a parent directory.
The schema is an object with a string email field and an explicit 'Invalid email address' message; the caller reads the first validation issue after safeParse reports failure.
The invalid input is an invalid email string; the valid case also checks that the schema strips an extra property. Other schema types and Zod integrations require recipient-specific tests.
actions: On the unsuccessful safeParse branch, replace the removed errors alias with error.issues while preserving the caller's response shape and explicit error message.
Keep the success branch based on result.data so that parsed output and unknown-property handling remain observable.
Exercise both valid and invalid inputs through the actual consumer; a successful request alone cannot demonstrate that the error-path migration works.
Replay with the recipient's frozen install and manager runtime, then verify its actual schemas, error mapping and response boundary before accepting the project.
verification: Assert baseline and repaired target return status 400 with 'Invalid email address' for the invalid email and that the issue path is ['email'].
Assert valid input returns status 200 with only the parsed email field on both package graphs; the unchanged target errors consumer also passes this valid-only control.
Restore error.errors and confirm invalid input throws TypeError on the target, then confirm error.issues still rejects invalid data through the intended response.
Run the same behavior under npm, real Yarn PnP and pnpm; reject a missing arm or missing PnP loader instead of falling back to a matching-version parent package.
Run the recipient's validation and actual transport tests when it exposes the result over HTTP; this fixture's response object alone is not transport evidence.

records.title: Preserve TypeScript 6 workspace declarations and runtime after removing baseUrl
records.summary: The three-package composite workspace builds and runs with TypeScript 5.9.2. The unchanged 6.0.3 build reports TS5101 for baseUrl; removing only baseUrl exposes TS5090 for non-relative paths targets. Removing baseUrl and making those targets explicitly relative restores the clean build, emitted-declaration consumption and executable result. Separate controls reject missing references, altered declarations and a failed rebuild whose stale JavaScript still runs.
conditions: The exact transition is TypeScript 5.9.2 to 6.0.3 using Node 24.18.0 and npm 11.16.0 with three linked npm workspaces: contracts, domain and app.
Each package uses composite project references, strict checking, declaration output, explicit rootDir/outDir, noEmitOnError and Node16 CommonJS emission.

An inherited config declares baseUrl: '.' with non-relative paths targets such as packages/contracts/src/index.ts; those aliases match real workspace package names with main/types pointing to emitted dist files.
The evidence covers this npm package boundary and solution build. Yarn/pnpm workspaces, bundler aliases, ESM conversion and the recipient's full source graph need separate verification.
actions: Remove baseUrl from the owning inherited config and resolve each paths target relative to that config, adding './' where needed to preserve the original target location.
Preserve project references and package main/types declarations so downstream projects consume emitted declarations and runtime imports resolve to the built workspace packages.
Perform a clean solution build before runtime acceptance. Do not silence the deprecation, disable strict checking or accept a successful execution of output left by a failed build.
Validate incremental propagation after editing an upstream contract and run the recipient's final workspace build and runtime checks before accepting the migration.
verification: Run clean tsc -b builds on the old graph and repaired target, then execute the built app and compare the USD receipt: subtotal 2500 cents, tax 188 cents and total 2688 cents.
Inspect the app's --listFilesOnly result: contracts and domain must contribute emitted .d.ts files, with their upstream .ts source files absent from the app compilation.
Delete the app's project references and expect TS6059/TS6307; change the emitted domain return declaration to Promise<Receipt> and expect TS2739 without editing its source.
Change the upstream tax constant from 750 to 1000 basis points, rebuild incrementally and assert the new declaration literal and runtime total of 2750 cents.
Introduce an invalid EUR currency and require TS2322 rejection even though unchanged stale JavaScript remains executable; then repeat the recipient's own clean build and behavioral acceptance.

records.title: Preserve browser transitions and focus during the coupled React 19 migration
records.summary: In the exact React/DOM/Router cohort, upgrading the old application makes react-transition-group 4.4.5 fail on the removed findDOMNode API. Passing the same stable DOM ref to CSSTransition and its child restores two real browser enter/exit cycles, visible panel state and focus return. A separate Router repair is also required for the intended sibling route; each partial repair leaves the other failure observable.
conditions: The coupled baseline is React 18.3.1, react-dom 18.3.1, react-router-dom 6.30.3 and react-transition-group 4.4.5; the target is React 19.3.0, react-dom 19.3.0, react-router-dom 7.18.4 and unchanged react-transition-group 4.4.5.
The fixture uses npm 11.16.0 on Node 24.18.0, esbuild 0.25.10 with the automatic JSX transform, Playwright 1.56.1 and Chromium Headless Shell 141.0.7390.37, revision 1194.

This is a BrowserRouter application with declarative routes, one unkeyed CSSTransition and local form state. Hydration, data loaders, keyed transition lists and other browser engines are outside the retained evidence.
Browser behavior is replayed at 1280x800 and an emulated 390x844 mobile viewport. The mobile case is Chromium viewport and touch emulation, not a physical-device result.
The baseline CSSTransition omits nodeRef, unmounts on exit and moves focus between its open and close buttons; a separate dashboard/* route contains a relative reports link.
actions: Create a stable ref for the transitioning DOM element, attach it to that element and pass that same ref as CSSTransition's nodeRef.
Review transition callbacks when supplying nodeRef: use the ref for the element and account for changed callback arguments; the retained onEnter check receives isAppearing rather than a DOM node.
Apply the independent Router repair where the same route pattern exists: split /dashboard/* into a /dashboard parent and * child, then use ../reports for the sibling link.
Replay the recipient's transitions, focus handling, route history and state retention with its supported browsers before accepting the coupled upgrade.
verification: Replay old graph/old code, new graph/old code, each single repair and both repairs at desktop and emulated mobile sizes; assert the specified failure or behavior in every arm.

Use the keyboard to type a draft, Tab to the opener, open with Space and close with Enter. Assert visibility and opacity 1 on the first enter; complete two enter/exit cycles with panel removal and focus returned to the opener after each exit.
Check the nodeRef callback's first argument and that the ref points to the panel; verify the form value survives relative navigation, an absolute-link control, browser Back and transition cycles.
Require both intended sibling navigation and transition success on the repaired cohort, no unexpected page errors, no external requests and no horizontal overflow.
Retain browser/tool versions, package and input hashes, emitted bundle hashes and screenshots; separately test recipient hydration, keyed lists and other browser engines when used.

records.title: Preserve browser sibling navigation during the coupled Router 7 migration
records.summary: With the retained coupled React/DOM/Router upgrade, a relative reports link rendered under /dashboard/* at /dashboard/team moves to /dashboard/team/reports and leaves the intended Reports page unopened. Splitting the parent and splat child and changing the link to ../reports restores the sibling URL, rendered page and browser Back behavior. The accompanying transition still needs its independent nodeRef repair.
conditions: The coupled baseline is React 18.3.1, react-dom 18.3.1, react-router-dom 6.30.3 and react-transition-group 4.4.5; the target is React 19.3.0, react-dom 19.3.0, react-router-dom 7.18.4 and unchanged react-transition-group 4.4.5.
The fixture uses npm 11.16.0 on Node 24.18.0, esbuild 0.25.10 with the automatic JSX transform, Playwright 1.56.1 and Chromium Headless Shell 141.0.7390.37, revision 1194.

This is a BrowserRouter application with declarative routes, one unkeyed CSSTransition and local form state. Hydration, data loaders, keyed transition lists and other browser engines are outside the retained evidence.
Browser behavior is replayed at 1280x800 and an emulated 390x844 mobile viewport. The mobile case is Chromium viewport and touch emulation, not a physical-device result.

A multi-segment splat route /dashboard/* renders Link to='reports' from /dashboard/team with the intention of navigating to the sibling /dashboard/reports route; the baseline does not opt into the v7 relative-splat behavior.
actions: Separate the named /dashboard parent route from its * child and change this sibling link to ../reports, preserving the intended /dashboard/reports destination.
Keep the absolute /dashboard/reports link as an independent control and inspect the recipient's nested/index route shapes before applying the same pattern elsewhere.
Wait for the expected rendered route as well as the browser URL when testing Router 7 navigation, because the URL can update before the React transition commits.
Repair the coupled CSSTransition with a stable nodeRef on the child and transition; then verify recipient navigation, browser history, focus and form state on its final tree.
verification: At /dashboard/team, click the relative link and check both /dashboard/reports in browser history and the rendered Reports page; use Back and assert the original route and retained draft value.
Run the absolute-link control in every arm, including the broken relative-route arms, so navigation availability alone cannot satisfy sibling-route acceptance.
Run all five old/new/partial/full repair arms at desktop and emulated mobile sizes. The new graph without the route repair must expose /dashboard/team/reports even if the transition is repaired.
Require both fixes to preserve keyboard entry, two transition cycles, focus return, form state and the intended sibling route without unexpected page errors or external requests.
Run the recipient's actual route, index, data-loader and hydration cases where present; the retained declarative Chromium application does not establish those broader outcomes.
